thread:
rachel: Quick synthesis from the hallway tests on the Credentials modal. Main pain: people don't grasp the difference between presets and manual toggles; rotate/revoke language feels too heavy.

tom: Can you list the smallest set of changes we can ship fast?

rachel: 1) Add inline preset pills (Embeddings, Read-only, Admin-lite) that expand a one-line summary when clicked. 2) Soft-revoke: mark as revoked in UI, keep tokens live for a 10m grace with visible countdown + undo toast. 3) After rotate, surface a short checklist and sticky copy CTA on mobile.

mina: For the pills, show the boolean flags when expanded? Users liked seeing exact effects (e.g., "cannot call /v1/generate"). Keep the expansion inline rather than a tooltip.

david: Agree. Also change "Revoke" primary to "Mark as revoked (10m)" and keep "Force revoke now" in a danger menu. That reduced anxiety in tests.

a11y-bot: Accessibility notes: when preset expands, set aria-expanded and announce the summary in an aria-live polite region. When secret is revealed, move focus to Copy and announce: "API key revealed. Press Copy to copy. This key will not be shown again."

tom: Copy wording for the broad-perms banner? Research preferred concrete examples vs vague warnings.

rachel: Recommended copy: "This key can create tokens and run model generation. Consider limiting scope or using a service account. Learn more." Short, factual, with a link to mitigations.

mina: Rotation UX: show the new secret in a dismissible banner with a prominent Copy button and three checklist items: update CI, update running jobs, rotate dependent keys. Make the banner keyboard focusable.

david: Mobile: when secret is visible, show sticky bottom bar with Copy + Dismiss. Also collapse the permissions grid into a single select when viewport < 520px.

rachel: I'll update the Figma frames and add annotated a11y notes. Can we pilot soft-revoke + presets behind a beta flag?

tom: Yes, pilot sounds right. Schedule a quick eng triage tomorrow to estimate.

rachel: Dropping frames into #design-review now. Thanks! :raised_hands:
